ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a circle with O as the center, point A is at the lower left of the circle, point B is at the upper right, and point C is at the lower right. Segment AB passes through the center O, therefore A and B are a pair of opposite points on the circle; the problem also explicitly gives that AB is a diameter of circle O. Arc ACB represents that arc from A to B and passing through C. Then reason: Because AB is a diameter, it divides the circle into two semicircular arcs, and the measure of each semicircular arc is 180°. Arc ACB is exactly one of the semicircular arcs determined by diameter AB, so m(arc ACB)=180°.

raw_record.question_text: $\overline{EC}$ and $\overline{AB}$ are diameters of $\odot O$. Find the measure of $\widehat{ACB}$.

method.method_draft: First inspect the diagram: A and B are opposite points on the circle with segment AB drawn through the center O, and point C lies on the circular path from A to B on the lower/right side. From the text, use the given fact that \(\overline{AB}\) is a diameter of \(\odot O\). A diameter cuts the circle into two semicircular arcs, each measuring \(180^\circ\). The notation \(\widehat{ACB}\) asks for the arc from A to B that passes through C, so it is exactly one of the semicircles determined by diameter AB. Therefore \(m\widehat{ACB}=180\).
